extraction.name: LUMA
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark dataset for learning from uncertain data, containing aligned image, audio, and text modalities across 50 classes. It supports controlled injection of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty and is accompanied by a Python package and baseline models for benchmarking.
extraction.creator: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was compiled by extending CIFAR-10/100 images with audio samples extracted and validated from three existing audio corpora, and text passages generated from class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct LLM; the modalities were then aligned so each text and audio sample corresponded to the image class.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data consisted of CIFAR-10/100 images, speech audio from The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice, plus text passages generated from CIFAR class labels with Gemma-7B Instruct; EDM-generated images were also included to increase image samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Audio samples were validated first automatically by transcribing them with Whisper Large V3 and checking whether the transcription matched the class label or plural form; samples failing automatic validation were manually labeled in Label Studio with a yes/no prompt by colleagues with advanced to fluent English knowledge, and only samples confirmed by both annotators were accepted while conflicting annotations were rejected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: They measured annotation agreement for manual validation and used acceptance/rejection rules based on agreement: 71.61% agreement, accepting samples where both annotators agreed the sample was valid and rejecting conflicting annotations.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 17 annotators who were colleagues: M.Sc. students, PhD students, and professors with advanced to fluent English knowledge.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI Whisper Large V3 was used for automatic validation/transcription of audio samples.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes a bias-related consideration in the audio modality, specifically accent diversity, and states that additional bias analysis was performed on the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current multimodal datasets are limited because they mainly repurpose unimodal data, lack controlled injection of different uncertainty types, and often use Gaussian noise that does not reflect real-world noise. For LUMA itself, only 42 classes have enough aligned samples for train/test, while 8 classes are treated as OOD; CIFAR-100 also lacks more than 600 samples per class, requiring generated images to alleviate this issue.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support development of more trustworthy and robust multimodal machine learning, especially for safety-critical applications such as healthcare, autonomous driving, and finance.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Accent diversity in speakers is considered in the audio modality; the audio data also comes from volunteer contributors from around the world, implying collection across geography/language communities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for learning from uncertain multimodal data, benchmarking and evaluating multimodal uncertainty quantification methods, debugging and analyzing uncertain multimodal data, and training/testing baseline models. Each generated version includes 500 training and 100 testing samples per class, plus OOD samples.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released as open source with code, instructions, a Hugging Face dataset page, and a GitHub repository. The authors state plans for future extension with additional and dependent modalities, and note that the open-source pipeline facilitates community contributions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Post-preprocessing dataset variants are generated by controlling data diversity through feature-based sampling, injecting modality-specific sample noise, adding structured label noise, and injecting out-of-distribution samples.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A clean version of the dataset with minimal uncertainty was first compiled. For modeling, audio samples were padded and converted to 128x128 mel-spectrograms, and text was converted to BERT token embeddings averaged into one embedding per passage.

name.evidence: We propose LUMA, a unique multimodal dataset

description.evidence: We propose LUMA, a unique multimodal dataset, featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for learning from uncertain data... The LUMA dataset enables the controlled injection of varying types and degrees of uncertainty

creator.evidence: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier.

publisher.evidence: The definitive Version of Record was published in Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR ’25)

datePublished.evidence: ACM Reference Format: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data.

inLanguage.evidence: The LibriSpeech dataset is a corpus of 1,000 hours of English speech

rai:dataCollection.evidence: “We compiled the images from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset [18], extracted, validated, and associated audio samples corresponding to the CIFAR image class labels from three diverse audio corpora [2, 15, 27], and generated the text modality based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct [25] Large Language Model (LLM).”

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: “It extends the well-known CIFAR 10/100 dataset with audio samples extracted from three audio corpora, and text data generated using the Gemma-7B Large Language Model (LLM).”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “The dataset includes 101,000 images, 135,096 speech audio recordings, and 62,875 text passages” and “we used The Spoken Wikipedia [15], LibriSpeech [27], and Mozilla Common Voice [2] corpora” and “generated the text modality based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct [25]” and “We alleviated this issue with including images generated with EDM Diffusion-based generative model”

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “The automatic validation was achieved with the OpenAI’s Whisper Large V3 model [29] for audio transcription... If the transcription corresponded to the class label (or its plural form), then we considered the sample as valid. Otherwise, the sample was sent for manual validation.”; “We opted for Label Studio [31] to build the labeling interface. The interface provided the audio sample, with the prompt ‘Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra ’s’ or ’es’ in the pronunciation is okay.)’ and answer options of ‘Yes’ or ‘No’.”; “We asked our colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge to annotate the samples.”; “accepted 5,027 samples, where both annotators confirmed the validity of the sample. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.”

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: “We opted for Label Studio [31] to build the labeling interface.”

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: “In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators. We got 71.61% annotation agreement and accepted 5,027 samples, where both annotators confirmed the validity of the sample. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.”

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: “In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators.”

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: “We asked our colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge to annotate the samples.”; “In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators.”

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: “The automatic validation was achieved with the OpenAI’s Whisper Large V3 model [29] for audio transcription, and transcribed the extracted audio samples.”

rai:dataBiases.evidence: "For audio modality, the diversity of accent in the pronunciation was an important factor to consider"; "We also performed additional bias analysis of the dataset."

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: "These datasets typically extract different features from unimodal sources to create a multi-view setup"; "they primarily repurpose unimodal data for multimodal tasks"; "Gaussian noise does increase uncertainty, it does not accurately reflect the noise that can be found in real-world datasets"; "42 classes were chosen so that after aligning with the other modalities, we would have at least 600 samples in each class per modality"; "We took another 8 classes, which had less than 600 samples after aligning with other modalities, as OOD samples"; "in CIFAR-100 dataset, there are no more than 600 samples per class. We alleviated this issue with including images generated with EDM Diffusion-based generative model"

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: "We anticipate that the LUMA dataset will help the research community to design more trustworthy and robust machine learning approaches for safety critical applications."; "In domains such as healthcare, autonomous driving, and finance"

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: "For audio modality, the diversity of accent in the pronunciation was an important factor to consider"; "The Mozilla Common Voice corpora, is a crowdsourced open-source collection of voices by volunteer contributors from around the world."

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: "a multimodal dataset specifically designed for benchmarking multimodal learning algorithms on uncertain data"; "To better understand and analyze uncertain multimodal data, as well as to debug and benchmark uncertainty quantification techniques in the multimodal learning context"; "Each generated version of the dataset consists of 600 data records per class (500 for training, and 100 for testing)"

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: "The code and instructions for downloading and processing the dataset can be found at: https://github.com/bezirganyan/LUMA"; "https://huggingface.co/datasets/bezirganyan/LUMA"; "In the future, we plan to include dependent modalities"; "The open-source nature of the data compilation pipeline and code for uncertainty and noise generation facilitates the integration of new contributions from the community"

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We prioritized flexibility, offering multiple options for controlling uncertainty through adjustable parameters such as data diversity, sample-level noise, label corruption, and the injection of out-of-distribution (OOD) samples.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: we first compiled a clean version of the dataset with minimal uncertainty... For the audio modality, we extracted 128x128 mel-spectrograms from padded audio samples... For the text modality, we extracted the BERT embeddings for each token, and averaged them out, so that we have one embedding per text passage.
